JBMC's counterexample nibble(m=15, offset=20) does not reproduce: the method returns true in the interpreter and the property holds on it. The path to it probably goes through what JBMC runs otherwise than the JVM, whatever its class path: stubbed-handler at UnsignedNibble.nibble:8: catch (java.lang.IndexOutOfBoundsException) catches java.lang.ArrayIndexOutOfBoundsException on the JVM, which the program may raise, but JBMC has no class file of java.lang.IndexOutOfBoundsException and its stub has no superclass, so JBMC does not know the exception's class extends it: the exception escapes the handler; throwing-initializer at org.apache.commons.lang3.Conversion.<clinit>: the initializer of org.apache.commons.lang3.Conversion may throw java.lang.ArrayIndexOutOfBoundsException, java.lang.NegativeArraySizeException, java.lang.NullPointerException, which the JVM gives its caller as an ExceptionInInitializerError, and later uses of the class as a NoClassDefFoundError (JVMS §5.5); JBMC gives the caller the exception as it is, and runs later uses as if the class were initialized, and catch (java.lang.IndexOutOfBoundsException) at UnsignedNibble.nibble:8 tells them apart; unmasked-shift at UnsignedNibble.nibble:7: shifts an int with >>> by a distance that may be outside 0..31: the JVM shifts by the distance's low five bits, JBMC by the whole distance, so it fills the value with zeros where the JVM does not
